evidence.title: Known cases of the Hodge conjecture
evidence.abstract: The Hodge conjecture is a major open problem in complex algebraic geometry. In this survey, we discuss the main cases where the conjecture is known, and also explain an approach by Griffiths-Green to solve the problem.

evidence.title: Further counterexamples to the integral Hodge conjecture
evidence.abstract: We study the integral Hodge conjecture in complex codimension $2$ and $3$ for approximations to the classifying space of groups of type A. In degree two, we prove a conjecture of Ben Antieau, extending his two counterexamples to a general family of groups. In particular, when reduced to a finite field, these spaces extend Antieau's counterexamples to the integral $\ell$-adic Tate conjecture from the cases $\ell = 2, 3$ to all primes $\ell$.

extending his two counterexamples to a general family of groups
records.falsifier: a theorem that all integral Hodge classes in codimension 2 are algebraic on these spaces
records.does_not_show: the full classification of such counterexamples, nor whether the rational form fails

evidence.title: A Lefschetz (1,1) Theorem for normal projective complex varieties
evidence.abstract: We prove an analogue of the Lefschetz (1,1) Theorem characterizing cohomology classes of Cartier divisors (or equivalently first Chern classes of line bundles) in the second integral cohomology. Let $X$ be a normal complex projective variety. We show that the classes of Cartier divisors in $H^2(X,Z)$ are precisely the classes $x$ such that (i) the image of $x$ in $H^2(X,C)$ (cohomology with complex coefficients) lies in $F^1 H^2(X,C)$ (first level of the Hodge filtration for Deligne's mixed Hodge structure), and (ii) $x$ is Zariski-locally trivial, i.e., there is a covering of $X$ by Zariski open sets $U$ such that $x$ has zero image in $H^2(U,Z)$. For normal quasi-projective varieties, this positively answers a question of Barbieri-Viale and Srinivas (J. Reine Ang. Math. 450 (1994)), where examples are given to show that divisor classes are not characterized by either one of the above conditions (i), (ii), taken by itself, unlike in the case of non-singular varieties. The present paper also contains an example of a non-normal projective variety for which (i) and (ii) do not suffice to characterize divisor classes.

quotes: We prove an analogue of the Lefschetz (1,1) Theorem characterizing cohomology classes of Cartier divisors
records.falsifier: a smooth projective variety with a (1,1) class that is not algebraic
records.does_not_show: nothing about codimension 2 and higher, which is where the conjecture is open

evidence.title: Hodge conjecture for projective hypersurface
evidence.abstract: We show that a Hodge class of a complex smooth projective hypersurface is an analytic logarithmic De Rham class. On the other hand we show that for a complex smooth projective variety an analytic logarithmic De Rham class of of type $(d,d)$ is the class of codimension $d$ algebraic cycle. We deduce the Hodge conjecture for smooth projective hypersurfaces.

quotes: We deduce the Hodge conjecture for smooth projective hypersurfaces
